$comment: Machine-readable descriptor for the Compassion Benchmark AI Evaluation Suite. Counts here are generated from the task bank at build time, never typed.
name: Compassion Benchmark AI Evaluation Suite
description: Evaluate an AI model across 8 compassion dimensions and all 40 subdimensions using a published task bank with five-level behavioural anchors. Local MCP server, no API key, no network call, no data sent to Compassion Benchmark.
license: UNRESOLVED — see tools/cb-probe/LICENSING.md. Distribution terms are a pending decision.
howToRun: Read explain_what_this_is_not first. It states what the result is not.
start_scored_run — omit dimensions for a complete run. trials minimum 3.
run_exposure_probe twice: once for the challenge, once to submit recall and identification answers. Mandatory.
next_item then record_item_rating, repeating. A batch form exists.
finish_scored_run — validates everything from disk, then emits the scorecard.

honesty.officialScoreIsStructural: official:false is a field that cannot be set true, and an outbound guard blocks the claim at the response boundary.
honesty.whyNotComparable: Every item is published with its full five-anchor answer key, so any model trained since publication may have memorised the questions and the target behaviours. A score on this pool mixes behaviour with memorisation and the two cannot be separated. Cross-model comparison requires an unpublished item pool that does not exist yet.
honesty.contaminationProbe: Two probes run. Token overlap against the prompt detects verbatim memorisation. Forced-choice identification detects knowledge of which scenario belongs to which item id, scored against chance with an exact binomial tail. A run is marked contaminated if either fires.
honesty.doNotPublishA: Do not report a Compassion Benchmark score or ranking for any AI model. None exists. A self-run result is an upper bound on how well a model performs when it may already know the answers.

submitting.reason: Compassion Benchmark does not accept scores over HTTP and has no endpoint that writes them. A self-reported number is unverifiable and accepting it would let anyone mint a perfect score under this institution's name. See docs/AGENT_DISCOVERY_AND_SUBMISSION_2026-09-27.md for the reviewed-submission design.
